manual:
GLOSSARY. **Shari** = `Gunkan Suship Shari`, the vanilla Level-4 2000-ATK Aqua every card in the deck asks for. **Topping** = the non-Shari Main Deck Gunkans (`Ikura`, `Shirauo`, `Uni`); each is the second ingredient of the Xyz named after it. **ED Gunkan** = a "Gunkan" monster you control that was Special Summoned from the Extra Deck — several archetype effects count these. **Shari bullet** = the "● `Gunkan Suship Shari`: Draw 1 card" line printed on all three Gunkan Xyz.

=== BIG PICTURE ===
"Sushi boat" = **Gunkan Suship**, a FIRE/Aqua Xyz archetype named after gunkan-maki sushi and warships ("Suship" = sushi + ship). Special Summon Level-4/5 "Gunkan" bodies for free, stack them into "Gunkan" Xyz Monsters, draw a card off every Xyz made with a Shari as material, and end on `Uni-class Super-Dreadnought` negating their board. The MasterDuelMeta Gunkan guide's honest framing: "The Gunkan Extra Deck monsters do not include a true boss monster, but all have utility and provide a free draw when made from a Gunkan Suship Shari."

**Core hub — Shari is everything.** `Gunkan Suship Shari Red`'s name *becomes* "Gunkan Suship Shari" while in the hand, Deck, GY, or on the field. Almost every Gunkan card asks you to reveal or use a Shari, so keeping a Shari in circulation IS the engine.

**One-card opener — Shari Red:** reveal another Shari in hand → SS Shari Red, then SS a "Gunkan" from Deck (except Shari) with its effects negated, and immediately Xyz Summon a Gunkan Xyz that *mentions that monster's name*, using it + Shari Red as material (a built-in Xyz that ignores the printed Level/Rank requirement). SS `Ikura` → `Ikura-class Dreadnought`; SS `Shirauo` → `Shirauo-class Carrier`; SS `Uni` → the Rank-5 `Uni-class Super-Dreadnought`. ⚠ This gives a free Xyz **body**, not a free draw — see EXTRA DECK rule (1).

**Extenders / search web:**
- `Gunkan Suship Ikura` — if you control a Shari, SS itself from hand; then excavate the top 3 of your Deck and add or SS a revealed Shari. Stack the top of your Deck FIRST with `Shirauo` or the Field Spell; otherwise, per the MDM guide, "you'll just activate and pray."
- `Gunkan Suship Shirauo` — SS itself from hand if you control a Shari **or an Xyz Monster that has Shari as material**; then SS another Gunkan from hand and put any number of Shari from Deck/GY on top of your Deck. ⚠ A `Shari Red` sitting as Xyz Material does NOT satisfy that second clause (MDM guide, explicit).
- `Gunkan Suship Uni` (Level 5) — reveal any Gunkan to SS itself; if you revealed a Shari, SS that Shari too. Separately, once/turn change a Gunkan's Level to 4 or 5 **and** add a Shari from Deck — that add makes it `Ash Blossom` bait (MDM), so expect the level-change to eat the handtrap.
- `Gunkan Sushipyard Seaside Supper Spot` (Field) — each time you Normal/Special Summon a Gunkan, put 1 Gunkan card from Deck on top of your Deck (the fixing that makes Ikura reliable). Defensive half: if the opponent sends your ED Gunkan to your GY, they pay LP equal to its DEF, then you SS a Shari from hand and Xyz Summon a Gunkan Xyz **using that one card alone as material** — a true one-card rebuild, and the reason to keep spare Extra Deck copies.
- `Gunkan Suship Catch-of-the-Day` (Continuous) — reveal a Shari, reveal a Gunkan Xyz from your Extra Deck, the opponent declares any non-Shari Gunkan name mentioned on any Gunkan Xyz, you add it from Deck. MDM: it "works like a `Pot of Greed`, since you get one card for showing a Shari and another for making an Extra Deck Gunkan Monster with that Shari." If the declared card is not in your Deck it shuffles itself away — so don't run a topping to zero while it is up.
- `Gunkan Suship Daily Special` (Trap) — reveal 3 Gunkans, add 1 (YOU pick if you revealed a Shari in hand, else the opponent picks); from the GY, banish it + shuffle 3 Gunkans back to draw 1. That recycler is what refills Catch-of-the-Day's declare pool.

**Generic glue:** `Rescue Rabbit` banishes itself for two vanilla `Shari` from Deck — they die in the End Phase, so ALWAYS Xyz them away at once (Shari material ⇒ the draw fires). `Unexpected Dai` SS's a Shari from Deck while you control no monsters. `Terraforming` finds the Field Spell. `Ash Blossom`, `Infinite Impermanence`, `Called by the Grave`, `Solemn Strike` protect the combo; `Pot of Desires` refuels.

=== EXTRA DECK (15) ===
Two rules govern everything you make here.

**(1) THE DRAW ONLY COMES OFF A REAL SHARI.** Every Gunkan Xyz has the Shari bullet, but `Gunkan Suship Shari Red` counts as "Shari" only *in the hand, Deck, GY, or on the field* — and an Xyz Material is in none of those zones. The MasterDuelMeta Gunkan guide states it twice: Shari Red counts as Shari "in almost every situation — It's not while banished or **as Xyz Material**," and, of Shirauo's "control an Xyz with Shari as material" clause, "Note that `Gunkan Suship Shari Red` as material does not fulfil that condition." So the Shari Red one-card line buys a free Xyz body; the DRAW comes afterwards, off the *vanilla* Shari you revealed, when you spend it as material on a second Xyz. (Disputed by casual players in a Master Duel Proficiency Test thread; trust the deck specialist, and treat a draw as a bonus if this engine rules the other way.)

**(2) BOARD WIDTH IS DISRUPTION.** `Uni-class`'s negate hits face-up opponent cards **up to the number of "Gunkan" monsters you control Special Summoned from the Extra Deck**. Every extra boat on the field is one more negate — which is why this deck stacks several small Xyz instead of one boss.

**--- The Gunkan boats (8 of 15 slots) ---**

**`Gunkan Suship Shirauo-class Carrier` (3) — Rank 4, "2 Level 4 monsters", 2200/250. MAKE THIS ONE FIRST.**
On Xyz Summon, in sequence, by material: Shari → draw 1; Shirauo → add 1 "Gunkan" Spell/Trap from Deck. (That on-summon block is once per turn BY NAME — extra copies do not re-search.) Standing effect: **while a face-up card is in A Field Zone**, your ED Gunkans — itself included — cannot be destroyed by the opponent's card effects and gain ATK equal to their **original DEF**: Carrier 2450, `Ikura-class` 2500, `Uni-class` 3400.
- *When:* it is the default `Shari Red` target. MDM: Carrier "is often the best target for `Gunkan Suship Shari Red`'s Summon from hand effect, immediately able to retrieve `Gunkan Suship Catch-of-the-Day`, again revealing the Shari used by Red to get the materials for a second Xyz summon, and drawing a card in the process to boot."
- *It arms itself:* the search fetches the Field Spell that switches on its own protection. Japanese reviewer みめっと on the Field-Zone requirement: "this is a search effect when Shirauo is used as an X material to bring [the] Gunkan Suship [Field Spell] and activate it by itself. Since you can meet the conditions, it won't be a tough condition."
- *Free ride:* "a face-up card in A Field Zone" is not restricted to yours. MDM: "The deck often doesn't find a field spell necessary, but your opponents' also work just fine for the minor attack increase and protection from destruction."
- *When NOT:* the protection is **destruction only** and dies with the Field Zone. Banish, bounce, shuffle-to-Deck, Kaiju/tribute, position changes and negates all walk straight through. Never build a board that treats Carrier as armour.

**`Gunkan Suship Ikura-class Dreadnought` (3) — Rank 4, "2 Level 4 monsters", 2200/300. The damage boat.**
On Xyz Summon: Shari → draw 1; Ikura → this card can make a second attack each Battle Phase. Standing effect: once per turn, when **ANY** of your ED-Summoned Gunkans inflicts battle damage, target 1 card the opponent controls; destroy it.
- *The pairing — make it beside `Uni-class`.* MDM: "the card destruction is most usefully paired with `Gunkan Suship Uni-class Super-Dreadnought` since it will be attacking directly." Reviewer タマーキン: "Ideally, use the destructive effect triggered by the direct attack of the Uni-class ship, and hit the two consecutive attacks after." A direct attack is guaranteed battle damage, so the pop is guaranteed.
- *Stacking:* the pop is once per turn **per copy, not by name**. タマーキン: "this effect is not the name turn 1, but the self turn 1, so depending on the situation, it might be possible to send out two Ikura-class ships." Two on board = two destroys.
- *Off `Rescue Rabbit`:* みめっと — "you can X Summon with only 2 Shari from Rabbit." Cleanest natural Ikura-class + draw, and it rescues the Rabbit bodies from the End Phase.
- *Going second:* two Ikura-class made with Ikura material = four 2200 swings. タマーキン: "when attacking second, if the opponent's hand is bad and the turn is passed on a blank area, from two cards in hand ... two consecutive Ikura-class ships — one kill is possible."
- *When NOT:* whenever you need removal RIGHT NOW. The pop is battle-gated, telegraphed and once per turn. Reviewer シエスタ (6/10): "the removal after the battle is easy to deal with before it is activated, making it difficult to handle. Since there are many other general-purpose rank 4 that can be removed at the time of the main [phase] ... it is not powerful enough to be general-purpose." Into an established board, take a generic Rank 4 instead.

**`Gunkan Suship Uni-class Super-Dreadnought` (2) — Rank 5, "2 LEVEL 5 monsters", 2900/500. The boss.**
⚠ Rank **5** — the only non-Rank-4 in the Extra Deck. Two routes: (a) `Gunkan Suship Uni` is your only natural Level 5, and its second effect makes another Gunkan Level 5 (that effect also searches, so it eats `Ash Blossom`); (b) skip Levels entirely — `Shari Red` SS's `Uni` from Deck and instantly Xyz Summons Uni-class off Uni + Shari Red.
On Xyz Summon: Shari → draw 1; Uni → gains the ability to attack directly.
- *The negate:* once per turn, **during YOUR Main Phase or the OPPONENT'S Battle Phase** (Quick Effect), target face-up opponent cards up to your ED-Gunkan count; negate their effects. **It is NOT usable in the opponent's Main Phase.** This is not a turn-1 combo-stopper; it is a your-turn board-breaker plus a Battle Phase trick.
- *The negate is PERMANENT, not until end of turn.* タマーキン: "Since this negate change is not for one turn but permanent, it is even more effective if you can negate a Continuous Spell Trap or a Field Spell that remains in the field." Point it at floodgates and Continuous cards first — those stay dead. Spending it on a monster you were going to run over anyway wastes it.
- *Main-phase use:* タマーキン: "if it's during the main phase of your turn, you can use it in a bully chain, so it works as `Marauding Captain` to attack while breaking through obstacles." Negate the blockers, then swing.
- *With `Ikura-class`:* みめっと describes the pattern — the negate "will erase the destruction resistance ... of the target card, and it will hit with this card to deal damage and remove the card whose effect has disappeared." Negate strips the immunity → direct attack → Ikura-class pops it.
- *Stacking:* also not name-locked. タマーキン: "The realistic number of ships that can be put out in one turn is 2, but if you can line them up, you can negate up to 3."
- *When NOT / limits:* it **targets**, so untargetable boards blank it; it sees only FACE-UP cards, so Set backrow is immune until it flips; and 2900 (3400 under Carrier) still loses to real boss bodies.

**COPY COUNTS — this list is heavier on boats than normal.** Across 20 top Gunkan Suship lists on MasterDuelMeta, players run **1-2 of each** Gunkan Xyz (Ikura-class in 19/20 lists, Uni-class 18/20, Carrier 16/20, essentially always at 1 or 2) and spend the freed slots on `Divine Arsenal AA-ZEUS`, `Number F0: Utopic Draco Future` and `Number 60: Dugares the Timeless` — none of which exist here. The 3/3/2 buys three things: more simultaneous ED Gunkans (bigger `Uni-class` negate), two pops from two `Ikura-class`, and spare copies to feed the Field Spell's rebuild clause, which burns one Extra Deck Gunkan every time it fires. The MDM author's counterpoint: without `Catch-of-the-Day` "you can comfortably drop to 1 Shirauo and Ikura" — this list runs 2 Catch-of-the-Day, so the extra copies are at least defensible.

**--- Generic Rank 4 toolbox (7 slots) ---**
All seven are **"2 Level 4 monsters"** — fully generic. Your legal Level-4 bodies are `Shari`, `Shari Red`, `Ikura`, `Shirauo`, plus any Gunkan `Uni` has re-levelled to 4. **The cost of going generic is the whole Gunkan package:** no draw, no bullets, and that body stops counting toward `Uni-class`'s negate. Leave the archetype only when a specific problem needs a specific answer. A Japanese reviewer's shorthand for how the classic toolbox divides up: "**Bagooska and Abyss [Dweller] for rank 4 disruption, Dugares for combos, and Castel for removal.**"
*(Legality note, since this list plays under the engine's `classic` format: three of these are hit on real lists — `Bahamut Shark` TCG-Forbidden (Apr 2025); `Abyss Dweller` Forbidden in the OCG (Jan 2025) AND the TCG (Apr 2025), and in Master Duel; `Number 41: Bagooska` Forbidden in the OCG (Jan 2026) and in Master Duel, still legal in the TCG. `Silent Honor ARK`, `Tornado Dragon`, `Castel` and `Exciton Knight` are unrestricted everywhere. Treat the bans as a power rating, not a rule here.)*

**DECISION GUIDE — opponent's board says → make this:**

- **They live off the GY (Tearlaments, Snake-Eye, Shaddoll, Burning Abyss, Mermail/Atlantean, Zombie, Dark World, Madolche, Fire King) → `Abyss Dweller` (1).** 1700/1400. Quick Effect, detach 1 as cost: your opponent cannot activate any card effects in their GY this turn. Yugipedia's tips name exactly those archetypes and add it "can be kept in the Side Deck for almost any Deck capable of Summoning a Rank 4 Xyz Monster." MDM's Gunkan guide: "a powerful Graveyard hate tool, **if you know your opponent is playing** Tearlaments or Snake-Eyes." TheDuelLogs ranks it the **#2 non-archetypal Rank 4 of all time**, "the most played rank four since its release" — and it is now Forbidden in the OCG (Jan 2025), the TCG (Apr 2025) and Master Duel, so having it at all is a gift of this engine's format.
  - ⚠ **IT IS PRE-EMPTIVE, NOT A NEGATE. Chaining it is too late.** r/yugioh's Q&A and Ruling Megathread: "`Abyss Dweller` does not negate effects in the GY, it prevents them from being **activated**. **If you Chain the effect of `Abyss Dweller` to an effect your opponent activated in the GY, then that opponent's effect will still resolve normally.**" You must fire it BEFORE they go for it. It also cannot be activated during the Damage Step (OCG ruling).
  - *So when do you fire it?* Default is the opponent's **Standby Phase** — Coalition of Scrubs: "nine times out of ten you're going to be activating that effect to detach material in the standby phase of your opponent's turn." Against a discard deck, go one phase earlier: "in their draw phase drop this card using its effect ... because once he's already discarded you can't actually stop the effects." The counter-argument (reviewer asd): "if activated during the opponent's Standby Phase, it may be stopped by `Infinite Impermanence`, and if you wait until the Main Phase, it may be processed by Kaiju, etc., so when to activate the effect depends on the environment and the opponent's Deck."
  - *Neat trick — enter the Battle Phase first.* From a Dweller-misplays video: "obviously you're going to detach and then attack, right? ... but what you actually want to do is to **first go into Battle Phase — by doing that you've made it so that your opponent can no longer `Effect Veiler` you** — once you're in Battle Phase, use Abyss Dweller's quick effect to detach." (Veiler is Main-Phase-only; Dweller is not. It still cannot be used in the Damage Step, so do it at the start of the Battle Phase.)
  - *The lock outlives the body.* Reviewer かどまん: "even if it is removed, as a residual effect after application he will continue to be GY sealed"; asd: "once activated, the effect remains during the turn ... and even if this card is processed, it is safe for the rest of the turn." Fire it, then stop caring what happens to Dweller.
  - *When NOT:* against a deck with no GY effects it is a vanilla — MegaCapitalG: "this card isn't going to be good if you're playing Geargia and you're playing against Dino Rabbit — but if you're playing against Dark World, what are you going to do?" Its 500 ATK clause is **dead here** — it pumps WATER monsters, and every Gunkan is FIRE. みめっと: "when used in a deck that does not use WATER, ATK is lower than that of a low-level attacker, and it is not uncommon for the status to be lower than that of the monster used as material." Literally true — you traded a 2000 `Shari` for a 1700 body. And asd's limit: it blocks GY *activations*; it "cannot prevent effects that interfere with the GY from outside the GY."

- **Your combo got stopped and you need to survive a turn → `Number 41: Bagooska the Terribly Tired Tapir` (1). GOING FIRST ONLY.** 2100/2000. In face-up **Defense** Position it changes all face-up monsters on the field to Defense and negates the activated effects of monsters that were in Defense when the effect was activated. It is untargetable and undestructible by the opponent's effects only in **Attack** Position — the two halves are mutually exclusive. Players call it "a walking `Skill Drain`" / "`Lose 1 Turn` but on legs."
  - *It is the compromise board, not the plan.* MDM's Gunkan guide: "a desperation play in case of `Maxx "C"`, but will often be negated or ignored entirely." Reviewer あんっ independently: "the most likely candidate to stop when hit with extra G [`Maxx "C"`]." A Superheavy Samurai guide puts the general rule plainly: "high impact handtraps like `Maxx "C"`, `Droll & Lock Bird` and `Dimension Shifter` completely stop the turn ... When that happens, make Bagooska to stall out your opponent until the time is right." Japanese reviewer カディーン: "a defensive move ... standing up as a substitute when the ideal lineup cannot be laid out."
  - *The lock is stronger than the text reads.* Both halves are Continuous Effects, so they use no chain and cannot be responded to. Official Q&A: a monster Normal Summoned in Attack Position "is immediately changed to Defense Position **before your opponent decides whether or not to activate its effect**," so the effect is negated; the same holds for a monster Special Summoned in Defense (Gagaga Cowboy Q&A) and for tribute-cost effects (Lonefire Blossom Q&A). Defense Position monsters also cannot attack, by rule. Yugipedia's tips list it as an answer to `Cyber Dragon Infinity`, `Shooting Quasar Dragon`, `Odd-Eyes Vortex Dragon`, and as a way to flip big low-DEF beaters such as `Blue-Eyes Chaos MAX Dragon` into harmless walls.
  - ⚠ **SUMMON IT IN DEFENSE POSITION, DELIBERATELY.** You choose the position when you Xyz Summon it, and a monster "cannot manually change its battle position for the rest of that turn" after being Summoned. Pick Attack "for safety" and you have forfeited the entire lock for that turn cycle.
  - ⚠ **IT LOCKS YOU TOO — and it will negate YOUR `Uni-class`.** "All face-up monsters on the field" and "monsters that were in Defense Position" have no controller restriction. Your own boats get flipped to Defense, cannot attack, and their **activated** effects — `Uni-class`'s negate above all — get negated. Never leave Bagooska in Defense on a turn you intend to negate or swing. Flip it to Attack on your own turn to unlock: reviewer カディーン — "since the defence by the permanent effect becomes a hindrance when you attack yourself, ... this guy simply changes the battle position"; フラクトール — "unlocking is very easy for a card of this kind," and Attack Position is also where its protection lives.
  - *It stops ACTIVATED effects only.* Costs still get paid and continuous effects still apply. Reviewer にしん: "monster effects other than permanent effects are blocked." A Rank-4 review video's worked example: `Card Trooper` "can still mill through his effect, however upon resolution that effect is negated"; `Amazoness Queen`'s continuous effect "will not be negated because it's something that you don't activate."
  - *When NOT:* ⚠ **it does nothing to Link decks** — Yugipedia gives both sides: "this card can be useful on Link-oriented Decks, as they will be completely immune to its second effect. On the other hand, **it is useless AGAINST Link-oriented Decks, for the same reason**" (Link Monsters have no DEF and can never be in Defense Position). ⚠ Don't make it against Superheavy Samurai, who attack from Defense anyway. Its protection is position-dependent: an official Q&A confirms that if the opponent chains a position change (e.g. `Zero Gravity`) to a destruction effect, Bagooska is in Defense when that resolves and dies normally — and every standard out (targeting removal, `Infinite Impermanence`, Kaiju tribute) works precisely while it is in the Defense form doing its job. Finally, the Standby detach is a **cost**, not an effect: with 2 materials it is a temporary solution of about three turns.
  - *Seat:* going FIRST. No source describes a going-second use for it.

- **The problem is BACKROW — especially SET cards or a Field Spell → `Tornado Dragon` (1).** 2100/2000. Once per turn (Quick Effect): detach 1, target 1 **Spell/Trap on the field**; destroy it. It is a free chain, not a trigger.
  - *Its edge over `Castel` is face-down cards.* TheDuelLogs: "**It can snipe face down cards unlike Castel**, but the real important thing about Tornado Dragon is its ability to do this as a quick effect ... **a way to take out set traps before they can activate is a very effective forward disruption.**"
  - *Field Spells are the headline target.* Dzeeff: "**Going first against any field spell deck this is a huge difference maker** ... you can just pop it with Tornado Dragon, **they don't get the search.**" It also hits Pendulum Scales (TheDuelLogs: "popping a pendulum scale or Spyral Resort before they could start off their combos was a great tool").
  - *Two uses if you cross the turn.* Reviewer asd, versus `Knightmare Phoenix`: "no hand cost required · **can be used twice if you cross turns** · 2100 points." Make it on your turn, pop something, then pop again on theirs.
  - ⚠ **CHAINING IT DOES NOT NEGATE.** Destroying a card in the chain only stops effects that must stay on the field to resolve. Per Konami's own FAQ (via Yugipedia's `Mystical Space Typhoon` rulings): Spell/Traps chained to are "not negated," and "may still resolve if they are in the Graveyard. However the effects of **Continuous and Equip Cards need to remain on the field to resolve, so their effects are not applied if they are destroyed.**" So chaining Tornado Dragon to a **Continuous/Equip/Field** card stops it; chaining to a **Normal Spell or Normal Trap does NOT** — the search/effect still resolves from the GY. (A popular Rank-4-toolbox video gets this wrong for `Tenki`; don't copy it.)
  - *When NOT:* against decks that play no backrow it is a blank — Cimoooooooo names Infernoid, Six Samurai and Dinosaur as matchups where "Tornado Dragon doesn't really do a whole lot," and warns that against decks whose Spells/Traps *want* to hit the GY it is "extremely inefficient and pretty much ill-advised to use in that matchup altogether." This deck already runs `Infinite Impermanence` and `Solemn Strike` for backrow interaction, and only 2 of the 20 sampled Gunkan lists ran Tornado Dragon — a narrow, matchup-driven slot. Never restricted on any banlist.

- **One FACE-UP thing must LEAVE and must not come back → `Castel, the Skyblaster Musketeer` (1).** 2000/1500. Detach 1: target 1 face-up monster, flip it **face-down Defense**. OR detach 2: target 1 **other** face-up card on the field, **shuffle it into the Deck**. Only 1 Castel effect per turn and only once that turn — you get one of the two, ever. Both are **Ignition Effects** and both **target** (official rulings), so they are your-Main-Phase-only and untargetable boards blank them.
  - *In practice it is the deck-bounce.* Reviewer かどまん: "the reality is that **90% of them only use the effect of ②**." Shuffling beats destruction-immunity AND denies the GY: Team APS — "**it doesn't destroy, so a lot of cards don't get to float.** Sending them back into the deck means that they won't be hitting the graveyard where they might be able to do some other problematic thing." ブルーバード adds that it "can deal with all Xyz materials" — bouncing an Xyz takes its materials with it.
  - *It answers face-up floodgates.* TheDuelLogs: "**Castel was one of the long-time best answers to problematic floodgates that love to remain face up** ... a great answer to other dangerous floodgates like `Anti-Spell Fragrance` or `Dimensional Fissure`." But floodgates that negate monster effects (`Skill Drain` and friends) turn Castel off before it can answer them.
  - *The forgotten flip mode.* It costs 1 material instead of 2, so it is the mode you can use on **two** separate turns. Team APS: "**this is actually the effect that a lot of people don't always think about. You can use that effect twice, whereas you can only use the spinning effect once.** So you can actually just use Castel simply to swing over a big monster rather than necessarily getting it off the field ... because Castel has 2,000 attack." The Aqua Duelist, on how rare it is: "**I honestly just never saw anyone use it.**" Note two limits: **Link Monsters cannot be flipped face-down at all**, and flipping an opponent's Xyz face-down does **not** strip its materials.
  - *Castel vs `Silent Honor ARK` — the comparison you actually want,* from Yugipedia's tips: "`Number 101` has 100 more ATK and can protect itself from destruction, but this card can target **Defense Position** monsters, as well as **Spells/Traps**. In addition, this card shuffles the target instead of attaching it, **denying any GY utility**. Since both monsters are valued for their removal effects rather than as bodies on field, this card is generally considered better." Team APS agrees and adds ARK's two blind spots: "this can't even take face-up Defense Position monsters. And it also can only take **Special Summoned** monsters." Reviewer やっつけ先生: "Castel has a higher range of countermeasures."
  - *When NOT:* it sees **face-up** cards only — against a board of Set traps it does nothing and `Tornado Dragon` is the pick (TheDuelLogs: "Castel's limitation to face up cards mak[es] it not so great against reactive back row"). After it fires it is an inert 2000 body. ⚠ Zero of the 20 sampled Gunkan lists ran Castel; it is here as a generic out, not a deck staple. Never restricted on any banlist.

- **One Special Summoned monster in face-up ATTACK position — especially a Link — is the whole problem → `Number 101: Silent Honor ARK` (1).** 2100/1000. Detach 2, target 1 **Special Summoned** monster the opponent controls in **face-up Attack Position**; attach it to this card as material. Plus a continuous "detach 1 instead of being destroyed" clause that the stolen monster then pays for.
  - *Why it beats destruction:* the monster is removed without being destroyed and without a leave-the-field trigger. Yugipedia's tips list `Evilswarm Ophion`, `Stardust Dragon`, `Mecha Phantom Beast Dracossack`, `Shooting Quasar Dragon`, `Elemental HERO Absolute Zero` — and an official ruling confirms Absolute Zero's mass-destruction effect does **not** activate when ARK eats it, nor later when it hits the GY. Attaching an Xyz Monster also dumps that Xyz's own materials to the GY (ruling).
  - *The one line to remember:* Yugipedia — "**This card's effect makes it a major threat against Link Monsters, since they are always in Attack Mode.**"
  - *When NOT:* it whiffs completely on Defense Position monsters and on anything Normal/Tribute Summoned, and it **targets**. Attack Position is checked at activation only — an official ruling confirms flipping to Defense in response does not save the target. Its 2100 body is unremarkable, and 4 of the 20 sampled Gunkan lists ran it (always at 1).

- **You are BEHIND on cards and the field has to go → `Evilswarm Exciton Knight` (1).** 1900/0. Quick Effect, during your Main Phase or the opponent's Battle Phase, **only if the opponent has more total cards in hand + field than you**: detach 1; destroy **all other cards on the field**, and the opponent takes no further damage this turn.
  - ⚠ **TIES DON'T COUNT — you must be STRICTLY behind.** A documented, commonly-made misplay: MegaCapitalG narrating a replay of a player who summoned it and then could not use it — "**you got to have less cards in your hand, you can't have the same amount of cards.**" Count hand + field on both sides before you commit.
  - *Mechanics:* it is symmetric — your own board dies too and Exciton survives alone. It does **not** target (OCG ruling), so targeting protection fails against it. The condition is checked at activation only: even if the counts change during resolution the wipe still applies (OCG ruling). It is **once per CHAIN, not once per turn** — with 2 materials you genuinely get two nukes in a turn, provided you are still behind after the first (OCG ruling). It cannot be activated during the Damage Step, nor at all in the opponent's Main Phase.
  - *Use the chain rule defensively.* YGO Stratz: "**you can chain its effect to its own summon, or if they activate a `Fiendish Chain` or `Breakthrough Skill` on its summon, you can chain its effect to that**, provided you didn't already activate it that turn."
  - *Why it is here at all:* MDM's Gunkan guide calls it "ZEUS' little brother," and Yugipedia's tips say when to still play it — "this card can be summoned and used in your Main Phase 1. If your Deck cannot summon Zeus ... then this card is still a good option for board wiping." This Extra Deck has no ZEUS, so Exciton **is** your wipe. Reviewer ブルーバード: "it can be differentiated from Azeus because it pops out from rank 4 **without going through battle**."
  - *Meet the condition on purpose.* ブルーバード's arithmetic: if the opponent kept ~6 cards and built a board, you "consume 2 cards and just put out Exciton," leaving your hand+field smaller than theirs — the condition is met precisely because you spent your own resources.
  - *When NOT:* when you are ahead — masterfox72 states it as a property of the card, not a tip: "**it is never a good card to use in a winning position. When you hold the upper hand in a game you will never consider using this card.**" Also note it counts RAW cards, not live ones: spent Continuous Spells and dead lingering cards still count against their controller, which is what makes it feel unfair. And the rider matters — masterfox72 again: "**no matter what, dropping Exciton will not end the game that turn.**" It is a reset, not a kill. Per reviewer gaya, "the number of cards with destruction resistance has increased recently, so it is no longer as reliable as it used to be."
  - *Pedigree:* TCG **Forbidden 2015-11-09 → 2018-09-16**, Limited to 2019-01-27, Unlimited since. The contemporary argument for the ban was not that the card was individually broken but that the generic Rank 4 toolbox as a whole was too strong and Exciton was the only member worth hitting.

- **`Bahamut Shark` (1) — ⚠ DEAD SLOT. It can never be Summoned in this deck.** Rank 4, materials "**2 Level 4 WATER monsters**" — and this Main Deck has **zero WATER monsters** (5x FIRE Aqua Gunkan, 1x EARTH Beast `Rescue Rabbit`, 1x FIRE Zombie `Ash Blossom`). Its effect is dead a second time over: it Special Summons a **Rank 3 or lower WATER Xyz Monster** from your Extra Deck, and there is no Rank-3-or-lower Xyz in this Extra Deck at all. Its famous package is **Bahamut Shark → `Toadally Awesome`** (Rank 2 WATER) in Mermail/Atlantean and Shark decks — Yugipedia's tips head its target list with "`Toadally Awesome`, to negate the opponent's card effects," and Bahamut Shark was Forbidden in the TCG on 2025-04-07 for cheating Toadally Awesome out without properly Xyz Summoning it. There is **no** "Bahamut Shark → `Silent Honor ARK`" package: ARK is Rank 4 and therefore not a legal target. Zero of the 20 sampled Gunkan lists ran Bahamut Shark. **Play as if your Extra Deck were 14 cards.**

=== TURN 1 (GOING FIRST) ===
You have no real endboard, so the goal is card advantage plus open interaction. MDM: "Going first, you'll be relying on non-Archetype cards to protect your board." Line: get a Shari on the field → SS toppings → make `Shirauo-class Carrier` with Shirauo material (search `Catch-of-the-Day`, or the Field Spell if you have none) → re-use the revealed Shari as material for a second Xyz and take the draw → add `Uni-class` if you can reach Level 5. Then SET `Infinite Impermanence` / `Solemn Strike` and hold `Ash Blossom` / `Called by the Grave`. **Widen, don't deepen:** 2-3 ED Gunkans = a 2-3 card `Uni-class` negate on your NEXT Main Phase. If the combo is interrupted or you eat `Maxx "C"`, bail out into `Bagooska` **in Defense Position** instead — but only if you have given up on doing anything with your own monsters next turn.

=== TURN 2 (GOING SECOND) ===
The better seat. MDM: "going second, the combination of the `Gunkan Suship Uni-class Super-Dreadnought` and the `Gunkan Suship Ikura-class Dreadnought` can negate and destroy a number of cards on their own." Sequence: build width first → `Uni-class` negate in your Main Phase to permanently switch off floodgates and protections → attack; Uni-class with Uni material swings directly, which guarantees `Ikura-class`'s pop. If that will not get through, take the generic answer instead: `Castel` shuffles the problem away, `Silent Honor ARK` eats a Link, `Tornado Dragon` clears the floodgate, `Abyss Dweller` before their GY turns on, `Exciton Knight` when you are behind on cards.

=== WEAKNESSES ===
- **Shari access is the deck.** Handtraps on `Ikura`/`Uni`'s search, or a Shari-light opener, brick it; `Shari Red` and `Uni` both need a Shari in hand to reveal.
- **The Field Spell is load-bearing:** removing it turns off `Shirauo-class Carrier`'s protection and ATK boost and stops the deck-stacking that makes `Ikura` reliable.
- **`Uni-class` cannot interact during the opponent's Main Phase.** Their whole turn resolves untouched; you only get your Main Phase and their Battle Phase.
- **Small bodies, no true boss.** 200-900 ATK outside the Xyz; the 2200/2900 boats are outclassed by modern bosses, and `Nibiru`, floodgates and faster combo decks beat you outright.
- **One Extra Deck slot (`Bahamut Shark`) is unusable** — see above.
extra: Number 41: Bagooska the Terribly Tired Tapir
